blocks.text:
# gh-1412: [GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done ## Description ## Goal — Near-miss elimination: the agent finishes, then verifies (v1) One sentence: **an unattended fa agent stops declaring success on intent and starts declaring it on re-verified state — the single-check near-miss class dies.** ### The data that frames this card (run 37736364517, final 43/80 = 54%) Of 37 failures, 16 are honest stalls (race-class, #1406), ~5 harness/task-induced (#1407/#1408), and **~13 are near-misses: the agent passes 4–6 of the task's 5–7 checks and loses on exactly ONE detail** — verified from parser verdicts: | task | passed / total | the one miss | |---|---|---| | pytorch-model-cli | 5/6 | final CLI output (chmod +x WAS done — the vim lesson generalized!) | | nginx-request-logging | 6/7 | index page content | | reshard-c4-data | 1/2 | the revert step | | organization-json-generator | 3/4 | relationships integrity | | raman-fitting | 1/3 | numeric peak values (G/2D) | | cron-broken-network | 1/2 | curl output CONTENT (file existed) | | vim-terminal-task | 4/5 | executable bit | | configure-git-webserver | 0/1 | left repo in post-test state | | build-linux-kernel-qemu | test crashed | verified with own initramfs, never the provided one | | hf-model-inference | 2/4 | model download incomplete (token discovery?) | | create-bucket | 0/2 | credentials declared missing after a shallow hunt | This is not a capability ceiling — it is a **verification-discipline gap**: the agent plans correctly, executes almost correctly, and never re-checks the produced STATE against the task TEXT before declaring done. ## Architecture Two named components, no new UI: - **FinalizeGate** (prompt contract, subject: the agent's own declaration of completion): in unattended/bench mode the system prompt appends a finalize contract — before ANY final summary, the agent (a) re-quotes every explicit requirement from the task text as a checklist, (b) verifies each item with a real command against the produced state (not memory), (c) fixes or explicitly reports every unmet item. Invariant: a final answer whose checklist is not all-verified is a protocol violation the harness can detect (see TaskLedger). - **TaskLedger** (session record, subject: the checklist itself): the checklist + per-item verification command/result persist as a hidden session record type (like `model_request_summary`), so (a) post-mortems can see WHAT was self-checked (this autopsy would have taken minutes, not hours), (b) the bench summary can report near-miss proximity ("failed 1 of 7 checks, checklist verified 6"), (c) CI can REG-gate the contract's presence in unattended runs. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
REAL command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[TaskLedger record
item, cmd, result] L --> FIN[final answer allowed] ``` ## Capability surface (what "verify before declaring" means — exhaustively) | capability | subject | shape | |---|---|---| | checklist extraction | the TASK TEXT (explicit requirements only: files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints) | agent-authored, quoted verbatim, one item per requirement | | state verification | the PRODUCED ENVIRONMENT (files, services, git state, processes) | real command per item; expected-vs-actual noted; no "I wrote it earlier" | | permission/executable checks | created scripts/binaries | `test -x`, shebang present — the vim lesson as a named item | | final-state discipline | the REPO/SERVICE the task describes | after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in | | canonical-artifact verification | the artifacts the task PROVIDES (initramfs, configs, URLs) | verify with THE GIVEN artifact, never a self-made stand-in | | credential hunt | the ENVIRONMENT (env vars, ~/.aws, ~/.hf, instance metadata, task dirs) | before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places; a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode means "hunt harder", not "give up" | | near-miss telemetry | the BENCH SUMMARY | per-task checklist-coverage line: items verified / checks passed | **Core (this card):** FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger record + bench summary line + the credential-hunt contract item. **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** harness-enforced gate (refuse to end turn with unverified items — needs a safe escape hatch for genuinely unverifiable items); contract + `credentialHuntNudge` actively direct the agent to probe credential locations
(`~/.aws/`, `~/.ssh/`, `~/.git-credentials`, env) and record verification commands and their
observed output in these very fields.

The repo's own convention (gh-1054 review, `_persistToolLivenessRecord` in
`agent_cli_persist.dart`) is explicit:

> Free-text fields ... pass through the host's redaction pipeline first: the session JSONL is an
> audit surface and must not leak secrets the in-run hooks already mask elsewhere.

The `task_ledger` record is an audit surface three times over: it lands in the session JSONL,
is broadcast to external hosts via the `task_ledger` wire frame, and is synced into bench trial
dirs (`agent-logs/fah-sessions`). Suggested fix, mirroring the sibling persister:

```dart
Future<void> _onTaskLedger(TaskLedgerEvent event) async {
  final session = _session;
  if (session == null) return;
  final pipeline = config.redactionPipeline;
  final data = pipeline == null
      ? event.ledger.toJson()
      : {
          'items': [
            for (final item in event.ledger.items)
              {
                ...item.toJson(),
                'requirement': pipeline.redact(item.requirement),
                'command': pipeline.redact(item.command),
                'expected': pipeline.redact(item.expected),
                'actual': pipeline.redact(item.actual),
              },
          ],
        };
  try {
    await session.appendCustomEntry(customType: taskLedgerRecordType, data: data);
  } on Object catch (error) {
    io.writeln(tuiError('task ledger persist failed: $error'));
  }
}
```

but it is exactly the class of record gh-1054 added the convention for, and the sibling
liveness persister already pays this cost. A regression test mirroring the liveness redaction

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind
#               under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom; the nightly macos leg
#               stays the main/tag backstop)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Reserve only —
      # ci.yml has no pull_request trigger (dispatch-only CI); the
      # flutter-app-exzone leg gates on the SM validation dispatch itself
      # (gh-1280 idiom) and consults this output only if a real
      # pull_request trigger ever lands.
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac

          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

# gh-1412: [GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done ## Description ## Goal — Near-miss elimination: the agent finishes, then verifies (v1) One sentence: **an unattended fa agent stops declaring success on intent and starts declaring it on re-verified state — the single-check near-miss class dies.** ### The data that frames this card (run 37736364517, final 43/80 = 54%) Of 37 failures, 16 are honest stalls (race-class, #1406), ~5 harness/task-induced (#1407/#1408), and **~13 are near-misses: the agent passes 4–6 of the task's 5–7 checks and loses on exactly ONE detail** — verified from parser verdicts: | task | passed / total | the one miss | |---|---|---| | pytorch-model-cli | 5/6 | final CLI output (chmod +x WAS done — the vim lesson generalized!) | | nginx-request-logging | 6/7 | index page content | | reshard-c4-data | 1/2 | the revert step | | organization-json-generator | 3/4 | relationships integrity | | raman-fitting | 1/3 | numeric peak values (G/2D) | | cron-broken-network | 1/2 | curl output CONTENT (file existed) | | vim-terminal-task | 4/5 | executable bit | | configure-git-webserver | 0/1 | left repo in post-test state | | build-linux-kernel-qemu | test crashed | verified with own initramfs, never the provided one | | hf-model-inference | 2/4 | model download incomplete (token discovery?) | | create-bucket | 0/2 | credentials declared missing after a shallow hunt | This is not a capability ceiling — it is a **verification-discipline gap**: the agent plans correctly, executes almost correctly, and never re-checks the produced STATE against the task TEXT before declaring done. ## Architecture Two named components, no new UI: - **FinalizeGate** (prompt contract, subject: the agent's own declaration of completion): in unattended/bench mode the system prompt appends a finalize contract — before ANY final summary, the agent (a) re-quotes every explicit requirement from the task text as a checklist, (b) verifies each item with a real command against the produced state (not memory), (c) fixes or explicitly reports every unmet item. Invariant: a final answer whose checklist is not all-verified is a protocol violation the harness can detect (see TaskLedger). - **TaskLedger** (session record, subject: the checklist itself): the checklist + per-item verification command/result persist as a hidden session record type (like `model_request_summary`), so (a) post-mortems can see WHAT was self-checked (this autopsy would have taken minutes, not hours), (b) the bench summary can report near-miss proximity ("failed 1 of 7 checks, checklist verified 6"), (c) CI can REG-gate the contract's presence in unattended runs. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
REAL command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[TaskLedger record
item, cmd, result] L --> FIN[final answer allowed] ``` ## Capability surface (what "verify before declaring" means — exhaustively) | capability | subject | shape | |---|---|---| | checklist extraction | the TASK TEXT (explicit requirements only: files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints) | agent-authored, quoted verbatim, one item per requirement | | state verification | the PRODUCED ENVIRONMENT (files, services, git state, processes) | real command per item; expected-vs-actual noted; no "I wrote it earlier" | | permission/executable checks | created scripts/binaries | `test -x`, shebang present — the vim lesson as a named item | | final-state discipline | the REPO/SERVICE the task describes | after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in | | canonical-artifact verification | the artifacts the task PROVIDES (initramfs, configs, URLs) | verify with THE GIVEN artifact, never a self-made stand-in | | credential hunt | the ENVIRONMENT (env vars, ~/.aws, ~/.hf, instance metadata, task dirs) | before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places; a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode means "hunt harder", not "give up" | | near-miss telemetry | the BENCH SUMMARY | per-task checklist-coverage line: items verified / checks passed | **Core (this card):** FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger record + bench summary line + the credential-hunt contract item. **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** harness-enforced gate (refuse to end turn with unverified items — needs a safe escape hatch for genuinely unverifiable items); checklist templates per task family (service-up, file-format, numeric). **Excluded (rationale):** showing the task's hidden tests to the agent (breaks bench validity); LLM-judged verification (non-deterministic, the whole point is command-verified state); auto-fix loops with >2 iterations (budget discipline — report, don't spiral). ## Pinned facts (from this run's evidence) - **P1**: near-misses cost ~13/80 = 16 points of score; even a 50% conversion → +6-8 points (54% → ~62%), larger than any other single lever except the stall race. - **P2**: the chmod lesson GENERALIZED within one run (vim-task missed it; pytorch-model-cli did `test_cli_tool_executable: passed`) — contracts travel once written down; the misses that remain are the ones NO contract names yet. - **P3**: stalls are concurrency-INDEPENDENT (16 timeouts at 2-shard 8-way in r2, 16 at 5-shard sequential in r3) — discipline fixes and stall fixes are orthogonal levers; neither excuses the other. - **P4**: `request_secret` decline in unattended mode currently reads as a dead end to the agent (create-bucket gave up in 4 turns) — the decline RESULT TEXT must carry the "hunt the standard places" nudge or the contract item dies at the first declined secret. ## Acceptance criteria (testable) - **AC1** — unattended/bench system prompt contains the FinalizeGate contract verbatim (UT: prompt builder asserts the contract block + its named items; absence in interactive mode asserted too — the contract is unattended-only). - **AC2** — a session that completes a task in unattended mode emits ≥1 `task_ledger` record containing every explicit requirement extracted from a fixture task text (IT with the fake-agent harness). - **AC3** — the ledger's verification commands actually execute (IT: fixture where the agent "forgets" the executable bit — the ledger item `test -x script.py` returns false, the fix applies, the re-run passes). - **AC4** — bench summary renders the per-task checklist-coverage line (UT on the summary builder with fixture ledgers). - **AC5** — the declined-`request_secret` result text in unattended mode includes the credential-hunt instruction (UT). - **AC6** — REG: currently-passing tasks do not regress (a 3-task smoke of previously-resolved tasks stays green with the contract on). ## Test matrix | id | tier | test | |---|---|---| | UT-1 | UT | prompt-builder: contract present iff unattended; named items enumerated | | UT-2 | UT | TaskLedger record round-trip (JSONL persist → replay → snapshot builder folds it) | | UT-3 | UT | summary-builder: coverage line from fixture ledgers, edge: no ledger → "checklist: none" | | UT-4 | UT | request_secret decline text carries the hunt nudge (unattended only) | | IT-1 | IT | fake-agent end-to-end: fixture task with 3 requirements, one deliberately missed → ledger shows the miss, fix loop runs, final ledger all-green | | IT-2 | IT | ledger absent (legacy session) → replay and summary degrade cleanly | | E2E-1 | E2E | re-run 3 near-miss tasks from run 37736364517 (vim-terminal-task, nginx-request-logging, reshard-c4-data) with the contract on: ≥2 flip to resolved | | REG-1 | REG | 3 previously-resolved tasks stay resolved with the contract on | | REG-2 | REG | full existing prompt-contract test suite green (no interactive-mode drift) | **CI rule: red REG blocks merge even when all UT/IT are green.** ## Non-goals - No showing hidden tests to the agent; `_onTaskLedger` persists `event.ledger.toJson()` verbatim, but every free-text field in it
(`requirement`, `command`, `expected`, `actual`) is agent-authored text — and the FinalizeGate
contract + `credentialHuntNudge` actively direct the agent to probe credential locations
(`~/.aws/`, `~/.ssh/`, `~/.git-credentials`, env) and record verification commands and their
observed output in these very fields.

The repo's own convention (gh-1054 review, `_persistToolLivenessRecord` in
`agent_cli_persist.dart`) is explicit:

> Free-text fields ... pass through the host's redaction pipeline first: the session JSONL is an
> audit surface and must not leak secrets the in-run hooks already mask elsewhere.

The `task_ledger` record is an audit surface three times over: it lands in the session JSONL,
is broadcast to external hosts via the `task_ledger` wire frame, and is synced into bench trial
dirs (`agent-logs/fah-sessions`). Suggested fix, mirroring the sibling persister:

```dart
Future<void> _onTaskLedger(TaskLedgerEvent event) async {
  final session = _session;
  if (session == null) return;
  final pipeline = config.redactionPipeline;
  final data = pipeline == null
      ? event.ledger.toJson()
      : {
          'items': [
            for (final item in event.ledger.items)
              {
                ...item.toJson(),
                'requirement': pipeline.redact(item.requirement),
                'command': pipeline.redact(item.command),
                'expected': pipeline.redact(item.expected),
                'actual': pipeline.redact(item.actual),
              },
          ],
        };
  try {
    await session.appendCustomEntry(customType: taskLedgerRecordType, data: data);
  } on Object catch (error) {
    io.writeln(tuiError('task ledger persist failed: $error'));
  }
}
```

The in-run hooks usually mask secrets before the model sees them, so this is defense-in-depth —
but it is exactly the class of record gh-1054 added the convention for, and the sibling
liveness persister already pays this cost. A regression test mirroring the liveness redaction
test would pin it."

blocks.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind
#               under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom; the nightly macos leg
#               stays the main/tag backstop)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Reserve only —
      # ci.yml has no pull_request trigger (dispatch-only CI); the
      # flutter-app-exzone leg gates on the SM validation dispatch itself
      # (gh-1280 idiom) and consults this output only if a real
      # pull_request trigger ever lands.
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:

          else

            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)

        shell: bash

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)

        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

# gh-1412: [GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done ## Description ## Goal — Near-miss elimination: the agent finishes, then verifies (v1) One sentence: **an unattended fa agent stops declaring success on intent and starts declaring it on re-verified state — the single-check near-miss class dies.** ### The data that frames this card (run 37736364517, final 43/80 = 54%) Of 37 failures, 16 are honest stalls (race-class, #1406), ~5 harness/task-induced (#1407/#1408), and **~13 are near-misses: the agent passes 4–6 of the task's 5–7 checks and loses on exactly ONE detail** — verified from parser verdicts: | task | passed / total | the one miss | |---|---|---| | pytorch-model-cli | 5/6 | final CLI output (chmod +x WAS done — the vim lesson generalized!) | | nginx-request-logging | 6/7 | index page content | | reshard-c4-data | 1/2 | the revert step | | organization-json-generator | 3/4 | relationships integrity | | raman-fitting | 1/3 | numeric peak values (G/2D) | | cron-broken-network | 1/2 | curl output CONTENT (file existed) | | vim-terminal-task | 4/5 | executable bit | | configure-git-webserver | 0/1 | left repo in post-test state | | build-linux-kernel-qemu | test crashed | verified with own initramfs, never the provided one | | hf-model-inference | 2/4 | model download incomplete (token discovery?) | | create-bucket | 0/2 | credentials declared missing after a shallow hunt | This is not a capability ceiling — it is a **verification-discipline gap**: the agent plans correctly, executes almost correctly, and never re-checks the produced STATE against the task TEXT before declaring done. ## Architecture Two named components, no new UI: - **FinalizeGate** (prompt contract, subject: the agent's own declaration of completion): in unattended/bench mode the system prompt appends a finalize contract — before ANY final summary, the agent (a) re-quotes every explicit requirement from the task text as a checklist, (b) verifies each item with a real command against the produced state (not memory), (c) fixes or explicitly reports every unmet item. Invariant: a final answer whose checklist is not all-verified is a protocol violation the harness can detect (see TaskLedger). - **TaskLedger** (session record, subject: the checklist itself): the checklist + per-item verification command/result persist as a hidden session record type (like `model_request_summary`), so (a) post-mortems can see WHAT was self-checked (this autopsy would have taken minutes, not hours), (b) the bench summary can report near-miss proximity ("failed 1 of 7 checks, checklist verified 6"), (c) CI can REG-gate the contract's presence in unattended runs. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
REAL command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[TaskLedger record
item, cmd, result] L --> FIN[final answer allowed] ``` ## Capability surface (what "verify before declaring" means — exhaustively) | capability | subject | shape | |---|---|---| | checklist extraction | the TASK TEXT (explicit requirements only: files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints) | agent-authored, quoted verbatim, one item per requirement | | state verification | the PRODUCED ENVIRONMENT (files, services, git state, processes) | real command per item; expected-vs-actual noted; no "I wrote it earlier" | | permission/executable checks | created scripts/binaries | `test -x`, shebang present — the vim lesson as a named item | | final-state discipline | the REPO/SERVICE the task describes | after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in | | canonical-artifact verification | the artifacts the task PROVIDES (initramfs, configs, URLs) | verify with THE GIVEN artifact, never a self-made stand-in | | credential hunt | the ENVIRONMENT (env vars, ~/.aws, ~/.hf, instance metadata, task dirs) | before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places; a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode means "hunt harder", not "give up" | | near-miss telemetry | the BENCH SUMMARY | per-task checklist-coverage line: items verified / checks passed | **Core (this card):** FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger record + bench summary line + the credential-hunt contract item. **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** harness-enforced gate (refuse to end turn with unverified items — needs a safe escape hatch for genuinely unverifiable items); checklist templates per task family (service-up, file-format, numeric). **Excluded (rationale):** showing the task's hidden tests to the agent (breaks bench validity); LLM-judged verification (non-deterministic, the whole point is command-verified state); auto-fix loops with >2 iterations (budget discipline — report, don't spiral). ## Pinned facts (from this run's evidence) - **P1**: near-misses cost ~13/80 = 16 points of score; even a 50% conversion → +6-8 points (54% → ~62%), larger than any other single lever except the stall race. - **P2**: the chmod lesson GENERALIZED within one run (vim-task missed it; pytorch-model-cli did `test_cli_tool_executable: passed`) — contracts travel once written down; the misses that remain are the ones NO contract names yet. - **P3**: stalls are concurrency-INDEPENDENT (16 timeouts at 2-shard 8-way in r2, 16 at 5-shard sequential in r3) — discipline fixes and stall fixes are orthogonal levers; neither excuses the other. - **P4**: `request_secret` decline in unattended mode currently reads as a dead end to the agent (create-bucket gave up in 4 turns) — the decline RESULT TEXT must carry the "hunt the standard places" nudge or the contract item dies at the first declined secret. ## Acceptance criteria (testable) - **AC1** — unattended/bench system prompt contains the FinalizeGate contract verbatim (UT: prompt builder asserts the contract block + its named items; absence in interactive mode asserted too — the contract is unattended-only). - **AC2** — a session that completes a task in unattended mode emits ≥1 `task_ledger` record containing every explicit requirement extracted from a fixture task text (IT with the fake-agent harness). - **AC3** — the ledger's verification commands actually execute (IT: fixture where the agent "forgets" the executable bit — the ledger item `test -x script.py` returns false, the fix applies, the re-run passes). - **AC4** — bench summary renders the per-task checklist-coverage line (UT on the summary builder with fixture ledgers). - **AC5** — the declined-`request_secret` result text in unattended mode includes the credential-hunt instruction (UT). - **AC6** — REG: currently-passing tasks do not regress (a 3-task smoke of previously-resolved tasks stays green with the contract on). ## Test matrix | id | tier | test | |---|---|---| | UT-1 | UT | prompt-builder: contract present iff unattended; named items enumerated | | UT-2 | UT | TaskLedger record round-trip (JSONL persist → replay → snapshot builder folds it) | | UT-3 | UT | summary-builder: coverage line from fixture ledgers, edge: no ledger → "checklist: none" | | UT-4 | UT | request_secret decline text carries the hunt nudge (unattended only) | | IT-1 | IT | fake-agent end-to-end: fixture task with 3 requirements, one deliberately missed → ledger shows the miss, fix loop runs, final ledger all-green | | IT-2 | IT | ledger absent (legacy session) → replay and summary degrade cleanly | | E2E-1 | E2E | re-run 3 near-miss tasks from run 37736364517 (vim-terminal-task, nginx-request-logging, reshard-c4-data) with the contract on: ≥2 flip to resolved | | REG-1 | REG | 3 previously-resolved tasks stay resolved with the contract on | | REG-2 | REG | full existing prompt-contract test suite green (no interactive-mode drift) | **CI rule: red REG blocks merge even when all UT/IT are green.** ## Non-goals - No showing hidden tests to the agent; `_onTaskLedger` persists `event.ledger.toJson()` verbatim, but every free-text field in it
(`requirement`, `command`, `expected`, `actual`) is agent-authored text — and the FinalizeGate
contract + `credentialHuntNudge` actively direct the agent to probe credential locations
(`~/.aws/`, `~/.ssh/`, `~/.git-credentials`, env) and record verification commands and their
observed output in these very fields.

The repo's own convention (gh-1054 review, `_persistToolLivenessRecord` in
`agent_cli_persist.dart`) is explicit:

> Free-text fields ... pass through the host's redaction pipeline first: the session JSONL is an
> audit surface and must not leak secrets the in-run hooks already mask elsewhere.

The `task_ledger` record is an audit surface three times over: it lands in the session JSONL,
is broadcast to external hosts via the `task_ledger` wire frame, and is synced into bench trial
dirs (`agent-logs/fah-sessions`). Suggested fix, mirroring the sibling persister:

```dart
Future<void> _onTaskLedger(TaskLedgerEvent event) async {
  final session = _session;
  if (session == null) return;
  final pipeline = config.redactionPipeline;
  final data = pipeline == null
      ? event.ledger.toJson()
      : {
          'items': [
            for (final item in event.ledger.items)
              {
                ...item.toJson(),
                'requirement': pipeline.redact(item.requirement),
                'command': pipeline.redact(item.command),
                'expected': pipeline.redact(item.expected),
                'actual': pipeline.redact(item.actual),
              },
          ],
        };
  try {
    await session.appendCustomEntry(customType: taskLedgerRecordType, data: data);
  } on Object catch (error) {
    io.writeln(tuiError('task ledger persist failed: $error'));
  }
}
```

The in-run hooks usually mask secrets before the model sees them, so this is defense-in-depth —
but it is exactly the class of record gh-1054 added the convention for, and the sibling
liveness persister already pays this cost. A regression test mirroring the liveness redaction
test would pin it."

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind
#               under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom; the nightly macos leg
#               stays the main/tag backstop)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Reserve only —
      # ci.yml has no pull_request trigger (dispatch-only CI); the
      # flutter-app-exzone leg gates on the SM validation dispatch itself
      # (gh-1280 idiom) and consults this output only if a real
      # pull_request trigger ever lands.
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac

      # root-level `dart test` ever discovers it — the fork's tests can rot
      # invisibly (that is exactly how the gh-1248 regression suite shipped
      # with a compile error). Run analyze + tests on the vendored leg,
      # where pubspec_overrides.yaml resolves the fork in-place.
      - name: Vendor fork tests (dart_tui)
        if: matrix.graph == 'vendored'
        run: |
          cd vendor/dart_tui
          dart pub get
          # Vendored third-party code: analyze keeps ERRORS fatal (the
          # gh-1248 compile rot this step exists to catch was error-level)
          # but pre-existing vendor warnings must not red unrelated PRs.
          # Plain `dart analyze` has no --no-fatal-infos (that flag is the
          # flutter tool's; infos are already non-fatal by default) — only
          # warnings need negating here. The test run below is the fatal gate.
          dart analyze --no-fatal-warnings
          dart test

  # SEC-07 (#795) AC4: run the installer against fixture releases
  # (good / tampered / unsigned) on EVERY PR — no path gating needed at
  # ~15s/job, and a security IT you can dodge with a cunning diff is not
  # an IT. macOS leg exercises the real quarantine-strip ordering (AC3).
  installer-verify:
    name: Installer verify IT (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:

      matrix:

  # gate live (network to github.com releases, read-only) on EVERY PR — no

  # gate's failure modes lives in installer-verify (contract 5).

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

blocks.text:
# gh-1412: [GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done ## Description ## Goal — Near-miss elimination: the agent finishes, then verifies (v1) One sentence: **an unattended fa agent stops declaring success on intent and starts declaring it on re-verified state — the single-check near-miss class dies.** ### The data that frames this card (run 37736364517, final 43/80 = 54%) Of 37 failures, 16 are honest stalls (race-class, #1406), ~5 harness/task-induced (#1407/#1408), and **~13 are near-misses: the agent passes 4–6 of the task's 5–7 checks and loses on exactly ONE detail** — verified from parser verdicts: | task | passed / total | the one miss | |---|---|---| | pytorch-model-cli | 5/6 | final CLI output (chmod +x WAS done — the vim lesson generalized!) | | nginx-request-logging | 6/7 | index page content | | reshard-c4-data | 1/2 | the revert step | | organization-json-generator | 3/4 | relationships integrity | | raman-fitting | 1/3 | numeric peak values (G/2D) | | cron-broken-network | 1/2 | curl output CONTENT (file existed) | | vim-terminal-task | 4/5 | executable bit | | configure-git-webserver | 0/1 | left repo in post-test state | | build-linux-kernel-qemu | test crashed | verified with own initramfs, never the provided one | | hf-model-inference | 2/4 | model download incomplete (token discovery?) | | create-bucket | 0/2 | credentials declared missing after a shallow hunt | This is not a capability ceiling — it is a **verification-discipline gap**: the agent plans correctly, executes almost correctly, and never re-checks the produced STATE against the task TEXT before declaring done. ## Architecture Two named components, no new UI: - **FinalizeGate** (prompt contract, subject: the agent's own declaration of completion): in unattended/bench mode the system prompt appends a finalize contract — before ANY final summary, the agent (a) re-quotes every explicit requirement from the task text as a checklist, (b) verifies each item with a real command against the produced state (not memory), (c) fixes or explicitly reports every unmet item. Invariant: a final answer whose checklist is not all-verified is a protocol violation the harness can detect (see TaskLedger). - **TaskLedger** (session record, subject: the checklist itself): the checklist + per-item verification command/result persist as a hidden session record type (like `model_request_summary`), so (a) post-mortems can see WHAT was self-checked (this autopsy would have taken minutes, not hours), (b) the bench summary can report near-miss proximity ("failed 1 of 7 checks, checklist verified 6"), (c) CI can REG-gate the contract's presence in unattended runs. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
REAL command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[TaskLedger record
item, cmd, result] L --> FIN[final answer allowed] ``` ## Capability surface (what "verify before declaring" means — exhaustively) | capability | subject | shape | |---|---|---| | checklist extraction | the TASK TEXT (explicit requirements only: files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints) | agent-authored, quoted verbatim, one item per requirement | | state verification | the PRODUCED ENVIRONMENT (files, services, git state, processes) | real command per item; expected-vs-actual noted; no "I wrote it earlier" | | permission/executable checks | created scripts/binaries | `test -x`, shebang present — the vim lesson as a named item | | final-state discipline | the REPO/SERVICE the task describes | after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in | | canonical-artifact verification | the artifacts the task PROVIDES (initramfs, configs, URLs) | verify with THE GIVEN artifact, never a self-made stand-in | | credential hunt | the ENVIRONMENT (env vars, ~/.aws, ~/.hf, instance metadata, task dirs) | before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places; a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode means "hunt harder", not "give up" | | near-miss telemetry | the BENCH SUMMARY | per-task checklist-coverage line: items verified / checks passed | **Core (this card):** FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger record + bench summary line + the credential-hunt contract item. **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** harness-enforced gate (refuse to end turn with unverified items — needs a safe escape hatch for genuinely unverifiable items); checklist templates per task family (service-up, file-format, numeric). **Excluded (rationale):** showing the task's hidden tests to the agent (breaks bench validity); LLM-judged verification (non-deterministic, the whole point is command-verified state); auto-fix loops with >2 iterations (budget discipline — report, don't spiral). ## Pinned facts (from this run's evidence) - **P1**: near-misses cost ~13/80 = 16 points of score; even a 50% conversion → +6-8 points (54% → ~62%), larger than any other single lever except the stall race. - **P2**: the chmod lesson GENERALIZED within one run (vim-task missed it; pytorch-model-cli did `test_cli_tool_executable: passed`) — contracts travel once written down; the misses that remain are the ones NO contract names yet. - **P3**: stalls are concurrency-INDEPENDENT (16 timeouts at 2-shard 8-way in r2, 16 at 5-shard sequential in r3) — discipline fixes and stall fixes are orthogonal levers; contract + `credentialHuntNudge` actively direct the agent to probe credential locations

observed output in these very fields.

The repo's own convention (gh-1054 review, `_persistToolLivenessRecord` in
`agent_cli_persist.dart`) is explicit:

> Free-text fields ... pass through the host's redaction pipeline first: the session JSONL is an
> audit surface and must not leak secrets the in-run hooks already mask elsewhere.

The `task_ledger` record is an audit surface three times over: it lands in the session JSONL,
is broadcast to external hosts via the `task_ledger` wire frame, and is synced into bench trial
dirs (`agent-logs/fah-sessions`). Suggested fix, mirroring the sibling persister:

```dart
Future<void> _onTaskLedger(TaskLedgerEvent event) async {
  final session = _session;
  if (session == null) return;
  final pipeline = config.redactionPipeline;
  final data = pipeline == null
      ? event.ledger.toJson()
      : {
          'items': [
            for (final item in event.ledger.items)
              {
                ...item.toJson(),
                'requirement': pipeline.redact(item.requirement),
                'command': pipeline.redact(item.command),
                'expected': pipeline.redact(item.expected),
                'actual': pipeline.redact(item.actual),
              },
          ],
        };
  try {
    await session.appendCustomEntry(customType: taskLedgerRecordType, data: data);
  } on Object catch (error) {
    io.writeln(tuiError('task ledger persist failed: $error'));
  }
}
```
